newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds lost ground on Friday, dragged down by floundering bund futures in the absence of any firm interest in the domestic market.

Dealers said trade was extremely thin throughout the session, with the tone weak at the opening and guilders fading away after bunds were hit by firm German regional inflation reports moderating hopes for a near-term Bundesbank rate cut.

With the long end marooned, the February 2003 state loan saw some business, but in general players were unwilling to get involved, one broker said. Weak U.S. treasuries piled on the pressure into the close, he said.
Guilders gained back a little on the spreads against Germany in the afternoon, but again underperformed on the day, with the 10-year spread sinking to end at minus eight basis points.

Dealers said the German data, combined with Bundesbank comment about steady near-term interest rates, would limit bunds in the next week and could also signal further trouble for Dutch bonds, with much now depending on the U.S. market. -- Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000, Fax +31 20 504 5040
